newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends easy, gilt prices mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends easy, gilt prices mixed.

text.p: Indian call money rates eased on good liquidity and moderate demand to end Wednesday at 0.5 percent, off the day's opening 1.5-2.25 percent, dealers said.
They said call money eased after the opening quotes on moderate demand as most banks seemed to have covered their positions.
"There were some quotes of 2.25 percent in the morning but rates came down as there were no borrowers at those levels," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
Dealers said most of the day's deals were done around 1.0 percent. Call money was expected to quote around 0.5 percent on Thursday, they said.
Dealers said prices of government securities were mixed in brisk trade. Traded volumes on Wednesday were 2.31 billion rupees against Tuesday's 2.20 billion.
"There was some movement in one or two stocks but most were little changed from yesterday's levels," said a dealer.

The 12 percent 1999 stock traded on Wednesday at 100.27 rupees against its last traded 100.18, the 13.50 percent 1997 eased to 101.53 from 101.55 while the 13.5 percent 1998 was steady at 103.25, dealers said.
Dealers said the treasury bill maturing on July 18 was traded at 9.65 percent against 9.70 percent.
Dealers said there was demand for long-dated securities maturing in 2006 but few deals were struck as there were no sellers.

"There is some punting that interest rates will come down after the credit policy is announced in the second week of April," said a dealer. "Some banks are tryong to trade on this but there are no sellers at the moment."
Dealers said some private banks had become active in the primary market for certificates of deposit.
"Some private banks are picking up three-month certificates of deposit at 12-12.5 percent," said a dealer. "But most of the large banks seem to be out of this market."
